rule: §9.2 — BF16 is permitted only if FP32 CUDA parity passes AND measured end-to-end throughput improves by at least 10% over FP32 CUDA (plus a 2,000-game zero-defect smoke and no evaluation regression).
why_not_bf16: BF16 autocast measured SLOWER than FP32 on the registered batch (0.1718s vs 0.1646s per update), so the >=10% end-to-end requirement cannot be met. The 2,000-game BF16 smoke was therefore not run: it could not change the verdict, and those games would have counted against the 124,000 hard maximum.
fp16_note: §9.2 prohibits FP16; it was never used.
torch_compile_note: §9.3 default is eager PyTorch; no compile benchmark was run, so compile is not used in the main experiment.
